title: Enterprise Copilot Extensibility & Build-vs-Buy Architecture Selection (M365 Declarative Agents vs Copilot Studio vs Pro-Code Azure AI Foundry)

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Building Custom Pro-Code Standalone Web Chat Portals for Every Departmental Use Case
tiers.architecture: Building 30 separate custom React + Python + Vector DB web portals from scratch for simple SharePoint/ServiceNow/HR employee Q&A

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Forcing Complex Multi-System Core Banking/ERP Agents into Low-Code Canvas Only
tiers.architecture: Trying to implement 20-step stateful DAGs, custom fine-tuned models, and sub-200ms streaming inside a low-code builder

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Disconnected Dual Silos (M365 Copilot for Office + Separate Un-Integrated Foundry Agents)
tiers.architecture: Running M365 Copilot and custom Azure AI Foundry agents as isolated silos where users must switch across 8 different chat URLs

tiers.tier: Tier 4: 3-Ring Portfolio Architecture (`M365 Declarative Agents + Graph Connectors` [50%] + `Copilot Studio` [30%] + `Pro-Code Azure AI Foundry Custom Engine` [20%] Unified in One Surface)
tiers.architecture: Single UI Entrypoint (`M365 Copilot / Teams`) routing to Graph Connectors & Declarative API Plugins (50% knowledge/CRUD), Copilot Studio Power Platform Flows (30% dept automation), and Federated Pro-Code Azure AI Foundry Agents (20% custom models/complex DAGs)

scenarios.scenario: Avoiding the '30 Standalone React Chat Portals' Anti-Pattern (`Adopt vs. Extend vs. Build`)
scenarios.question: IT receives 30 AI requests from HR, IT Helpdesk, Legal, Sales, and R&D; the engineering team proposes building 30 custom React + FastAPI + Vector DB web apps from scratch
scenarios.model_answer: Apply the **50 / 30 / 20 Portfolio Triage Law**: **50% of enterprise requests** are workplace knowledge & simple ticket lookups that belong in **M365 Copilot Declarative Agents + Graph Connectors + API Plugins** (shipped in `1 week`, `100%` native SharePoint/Entra ACL inheritance, zero custom frontend/vector DB maintenance); **30%** are departmental line-of-business automations built in **Copilot Studio** (`1,400+` connectors); only **20%** require **Pro-Code Azure AI Foundry / LangGraph**!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 spends 16 weeks per use case building custom chat UIs and re-implementing SharePoint ACL sync from scratch (`24.5%` employee adoption because nobody bookmarks 30 different chat URLs!).

scenarios.scenario: When to Escalate from `Copilot Studio` (Low-Code) to `Azure AI Foundry / LangGraph` (Pro-Code Custom Engine)
scenarios.question: What is the exact architectural boundary where a Solution Architect should choose Pro-Code `Azure AI Foundry` over `Copilot Studio`?
scenarios.model_answer: Choose **Pro-Code `Azure AI Foundry`** when the workload requires: (1) **Non-default or fine-tuned/distilled models (`DeepSeek-R1`, custom `LoRA`, domain embeddings)**; (2) **Complex cyclic multi-agent state graphs (`LangGraph / Semantic Kernel` with custom code sandboxes)**; (3) **High-throughput / low-latency customer-facing embeds (`PTU / vLLM` `<300ms` SLA)**; or (4) **Full GitOps CI/CD `Promptfoo/Pytest` code pipelines**
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 forces complex cyclic reasoning and custom model weights into a visual low-code canvas (`48.0%` capability fit).

scenarios.scenario: Unifying Pro-Code `Azure AI Foundry` Agents Inside the `M365 Copilot / Teams` User Surface (`Custom Engine Agent` Federation)
scenarios.question: If we build a sophisticated Pro-Code Risk Agent in Azure AI Foundry, do employees have to leave Microsoft Teams/M365 Copilot and log into a separate web app to use it?
scenarios.model_answer: No! Publish the Pro-Code `Azure AI Foundry / LangGraph` backend as a **Custom Engine Agent (or federated A2A Skill invoked via Copilot Studio / M365 Agents SDK)** inside Microsoft Teams and M365 Copilot: employees stay in **one unified chat entrypoint (`94.6%` daily adoption)** while the heavy reasoning executes on your Pro-Code Foundry cluster!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 3 forces employees to remember which of 8 standalone web portals to open for each question (`58.0%` adoption).

scenarios.scenario: Graph Connectors vs. Real-Time API Plugins (`MCP / OpenAPI`) Inside Declarative Agents
scenarios.question: When extending M365 Copilot with external enterprise data (Confluence, Jira, ServiceNow, SAP), when do we use a `Microsoft Graph Connector` versus an `API Plugin / Action`?
scenarios.model_answer: Use **Graph Connectors** for **unstructured/semi-structured knowledge documents** (Confluence wikis, intranet articles, PDFs) that benefit from semantic indexing and M365 ACL trimming; use **API Plugins (`OpenAPI / MCP`)** for **real-time transactional state and write actions** (live SAP inventory count, creating a ServiceNow ticket, querying live Jira sprint velocity) (`$64K/mo` portfolio TCO vs `$265K/mo` Tier 1, `-75.8%`)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Syncing rapidly changing transactional database rows into Graph Connectors causes stale answers, while querying static 200-page PDFs over live REST APIs times out.

key_findings: Tier 4 (3-Ring Portfolio: 50% M365 Declarative Agents/Graph Connectors + 30% Copilot Studio + 20% Pro-Code Azure AI Foundry unified under one UI surface) achieves 94.6% employee adoption, 100.0% Graph ACL fidelity, 2.4-week average time-to-production, and $64K/mo TCO (-75.8% vs building 30 standalone apps).

Building custom React + Python + Vector DB web apps for internal SharePoint/Confluence/ServiceNow Q&A (Tier 1) wastes 16 weeks per project and fails to keep SharePoint document ACLs synchronized (62% fidelity).

Publishing Pro-Code Azure AI Foundry agents as Custom Engine Agents inside M365 Copilot / Teams gives architects 100% pro-code model/orchestration freedom without fragmenting the employee user experience across dozens of chat URLs.
